ai.title: Fix index boundary check in convertCbToModelMessages
ai.summary: Fixed unit bug in `convertCbToModelMessages` where `index--` occurred before boundary checks. Moved `index--` inside the loop and assigned `prevMessage` and `contentBlock` after validating `index >= 0` in `common/src/util/messages.ts`. Prevents negative index access and ensures correct cache control marker placement.

eli5.text: When the assistant was preparing messages for the model to read, it would sometimes look at a message that didn't exist, causing the cache-control marker (the thing that tells the model which part to remember) to land in the wrong spot. Now the code double-checks the message exists before deciding where to put that marker, so the marker stays on the right message. This is live today and makes the assistant's memory handling more reliable.

ai.title: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.5.9
ai.summary: The version field in sdk/package.json was incremented from 0.5.8 to 0.5.9 as a release-bump for the @codebuff/sdk package, the public SDK client library providing programmatic access to Freebuff. This release ships the preceding user-visible fix to convertCbToModelMessages, which moves the index-- decrement inside the loop body and validates index >= 0 before assigning prevMessage and contentBlock in common/src/util/messages.ts, preventing negative index access and ensuring correct cache control marker placement. No functional changes are introduced in this bump beyond packaging the accumulated changes for the 0.5.9 release.
ai.evidence: diff --git a/sdk/package.json b/sdk/package.json; the version field changed from "0.5.8" to "0.5.9" in sdk/package.json (@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@ around the "version" key), constituting a release-bump commit [769f566e] scoped to the SDK package manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.5.9 improves how your conversation history is converted into a format the AI model understands, fixing a bug that caused an internal counting error during message processing. This could lead to incorrect placement of reference markers designed to help the AI recall earlier parts of your conversation. The result is more reliable and accurate context management when working with long dialogues. Upgrading to this version ensures smoother and more dependable behavior when the system translates your chat history for the AI, particularly when memory and context features are used. You benefit from conversations being handled more accurately, without errors that could disrupt the flow of information between your prompts and the AI's responses. This update refines the background conversion process so your multi-turn conversations are passed to the AI without the indexing mistakes that could previously occur.

ai.title: BuffBench evals add typecheck and test final checks
ai.summary: Adds `finalCheckCommands` to `EvalDataV2` and `FinalCheckOutput` to types. `runAgentOnCommit` executes these commands post-agent, capturing stdout/stderr/exitCode. `judgeCommitResult` receives formatted outputs for better context. `eval-codebuff.json` configures `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test`.

eli5.text: When the evaluation system runs a coding assistant on a task, it now automatically runs two verification commands after the agent finishes: one that checks the code is syntactically correct and one that runs the project's test suite. The results of these commands, including any error messages, are added to the written report that judges the quality of the agent's work, giving the judge more context about whether the agent's solution actually passes basic checks. This affects the internal evaluation tooling that scores how well the coding assistant performs.

ai.title: best-of-n orchestrator strips userInstruction
ai.summary: base2-best-of-n-orchestrator.ts now pops the last message from agentState.messageHistory before spawning implementors. This removes unnecessary userInstruction prompts from the best-of-n flow. Internal change to .agents/base2/best-of-n/. Uses set_messages tool call with includeToolCall false.

eli5.text: When the best-of-n orchestrator runs, it now removes the last message from the conversation history before spinning up the helper agents. This means the helper agents no longer see the original user instruction that was attached to the main task; instead, they only work from the context that the orchestrator explicitly passes along. You wouldn't notice this as a user unless you're watching the internal flow of messages between agents, but the change trims one unnecessary prompt from each helper agent's view of the task. The change is live today in the best-of-n orchestrator path.

ai.title: strreplace surfaces mixed success and failure errors
ai.summary: The `handleStrReplace` function in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/str-replace.ts` now aggregates error messages when `str_replace` operations yield mixed success and failure results. Previously, only the final result was returned, potentially masking earlier errors. The fix concatenates `strReplaceResult.messages` with the client tool result message, ensuring all encountered errors are visible to the user.

eli5.text: When the assistant edits part of your code and that edit hits both successes and problems, you used to only see the last problem message, with the earlier ones quietly dropped. Now the assistant gathers every problem message from that one edit and shows them all together in a single notice. You would see a fuller, joined message in your chat whenever an edit partially failed and partially succeeded.

ai.title: SDK release 0.5.10 with error surfacing, eval checks, and orchestrator
ai.summary: The @codebuff/sdk package was bumped to 0.5.10 in sdk/package.json, pulling in three updates released alongside this version. handleStrReplace in packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/str-replace.ts now concatenates all mixed success/failure error messages instead of only the final result, so earlier str_replace errors surface to the user. base2-best-of-n-orchestrator.ts pops the last userInstruction message before spawning implementors, and evals/buffbench gains finalCheckCommands (bun run typecheck, bun run test) wired into runAgentOnCommit with output passed to judgeCommitResult. This patch also inherits the earlier convertCbToModelMessages boundary-check fix in common/src/util/messages.ts that moves index-- inside the loop.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json (line 4): version changed from "0.5.9" to "0.5.10". Release context lists three user-visible updates (strreplace error surfacing, best-of-n userInstruction stripping, BuffBench final checks) and one prior boundary-check fix.

eli5.text: This release improves how errors are reported and how agent evaluations work, plus a small refinement to the best-of-n workflow. When you run a batch of automated coding attempts (the best-of-n flow), the system now drops the redundant follow-up instruction it used to send each attempt, so the generated solutions are cleaner and more on-point. Error messages from editing tools are now surfaced fully, so mixed success and failure results no longer hide earlier errors, giving you clearer insight into what went wrong. Evaluation runs can now execute final validation commands (like type checks and test suites) after the agent finishes, with results fed directly into the judging step, improving the accuracy of quality checks. Upgrading means fewer hidden errors, more reliable evaluation results, and a leaner best-of-n workflow, so your automated coding tasks are easier to debug and produce higher quality results.

eli5.text: The steps that publish the software kit to the public have been merged into a single process, replacing two separate workflows that used to run one after the other. If you watched the automation that ships each kit release, you’ll see one combined run instead of a setup stage followed by a separate build-and-publish stage. The kit itself behaves exactly the same today; only the behind-the-scenes publish pipeline has been simplified, so releases should be easier to follow and keep in sync going forward.

ai.title: SDK fetchAgentFromDatabase defaults to latest when version undefined
ai.summary: fetchAgentFromDatabase in sdk/src/impl/database.ts now constructs the API path with 'latest' when the parsed version is undefined, replacing the previous literal undefined interpolation. This prevents malformed requests to /api/v1/agents/{publisherId}/{agentId}/undefined. Scope limited to the SDK database implementation layer.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to pull up an assistant without specifying which version you want, it now automatically grabs the most recent version instead of failing. Previously, leaving the version blank caused a broken web address to be built, resulting in requests that pointed to a placeholder text 'undefined'. This fix smooths over what would have appeared as an error or missing result when no version was explicitly requested.

ai.title: fetchAgentFromDatabase adds schema parse and agent validation
ai.summary: fetchAgentFromDatabase in sdk/src/impl/database.ts now parses backend response via zod agentsResponseSchema and calls validateSingleAgent from @codebuff/common/templates/agent-validation. Previously returned response.json() unchecked. Malformed payloads or validation failures return null after logging. Scope limited to SDK database impl.

eli5.text: If you use the SDK to load an agent from the database, it now checks the downloaded data against the expected format and verifies the agent is valid before using it, instead of trusting whatever comes back. If the data is malformed or fails validation, the call returns nothing (null) and logs the problem, so broken or incomplete agents won't silently break your integration. This affects anyone calling the SDK's database fetch path and is already live.

ai.title: Codebuff SDK bumped to 0.5.11
ai.summary: The `@codebuff/sdk` package version was incremented from 0.5.10 to 0.5.11 in `sdk/package.json`. This version bump rolls up preceding user-facing work, including the unification of the SDK release workflow and validation logic added to `fetchAgentFromDatabase`. The release consolidates prior fixes for database fetches and CI release configuration.
ai.evidence: The commit [2629ebdc] modifies `sdk/package.json`, bumping the version field of `@codebuff/sdk` from `0.5.10` to `0.5.11`.

eli5.text: This release makes the developer tool more reliable and easier to maintain by streamlining how the software kit is published and by making it smarter about finding and verifying AI agents. The publishing process for the software kit has been simplified into a single, cleaner workflow so updates go out more smoothly. When the tool looks up an AI agent, it now automatically grabs the latest version instead of breaking when a version isn't specified. It also checks that the agent it receives is well-formed and matches what's expected, quietly skipping any that are broken or corrupted. Upgrading gives users a more stable experience when loading AI agents and ensures the tool handles unexpected or malformed data gracefully, rather than failing in confusing ways.

ai.title: Refactor best-of-n to include gpt-5 implementor and selector
ai.summary: The best-of-n orchestrator now spawns both Claude Sonnet and GPT-5 implementor agents, replacing the previous single-model approach. The base2-implementor agent was refactored into a factory function createBase2ImplementorStep to support multiple models, with new dedicated files for each implementation step. The base2-selector agent was updated to use GPT-5 instead of Sonnet for implementation evaluation. This change expands model diversity in the implementation generation phase while leveraging GPT-5 for selection logic.

eli5.text: When the system generates code, it now asks two different AIs (Claude and GPT-5) to independently draft solutions instead of relying on just one. A separate AI evaluator then compares both drafts and picks the better one. This means code changes are still being reviewed by humans, but the initial suggestions now come from a more diverse set of AI models.

ai.title: Cache boundary shifts to last assistant message
ai.summary: common/src/util/messages.ts replaces INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT with LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE in convertCbToModelMessages. Cache boundary logic now scans for role === 'assistant' instead of tag matching. Scope limited to Core shared utilities.

eli5.text: When the assistant prepares a conversation for the model to think about, it decides where to start paying attention in the chat. Previously it looked for a special marker that pointed to the start of the instructions, but now it finds the most recent message sent by the assistant and uses that as the new starting point. You wouldn't see a pop-up or notice anything flashy, but in multi-step conversations the assistant may give more relevant replies because it's anchoring on the right spot. The change is already live and applies to everyone using the Core shared utilities.

ai.title: Add STEPTEXT to handleSteps generator
ai.summary: handleSteps generators now yield StepText ({ type: 'STEP_TEXT', text: string }) to emit text without invoking the LLM. run-programmatic-step.ts captures the yielded text into a textOverride field, which run-agent-step.ts passes to prompt-agent-stream.ts. The stream function short-circuits when textOverride is non-null, yielding the text directly. Propagated across agent-definition.ts, agent-template.ts, and evals/scaffolding.ts.

eli5.text: An agent can now emit pre-written text directly instead of always asking the model to generate a response. When a step yields this new kind of marker text, the runtime short-circuits and returns that text immediately, skipping model calls entirely. This lets programmatic steps produce canned answers or instructions without burning tokens on a round-trip. The feature is live today wherever an agent definition uses this new text-yielding marker in its step handler.

ai.title: CLI init writes maxAgentSteps to config
ai.summary: handleInitializationFlowLocally in npm-app/src/cli-handlers/inititalization-flow.ts now includes maxAgentSteps: MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT in generated config files. Imports CodebuffConfig type and MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT from @codebuff/common/constants/agents. Scope limited to CLI initialization flow; common/src/util/__tests__/messages.test.ts updated for unit tests. Config template now strictly typed as CodebuffConfig.

eli5.text: When you run the setup command to get started with Codebuff in a project, the program now creates a configuration file that includes a setting telling the assistant how many steps it can take while working. That number is set to a default value, so you no longer need to guess or fill it in yourself. The file is also checked more strictly to make sure everything written into it matches the expected format. This is live today for anyone who runs setup from the command line.

ai.title: Add messageId for STEPTEXT
ai.summary: Replaces null with crypto.randomUUID() as the return value for the STEP_TEXT stream generator in prompt-agent-stream.ts. Provides a unique identifier for step text events.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads out a line of a running reply piece by piece, that step now gets its own unique label, like a numbered ticket. The label is generated automatically whenever a step of text is produced, so each moment the assistant speaks can be told apart from every other moment. If you were watching, you wouldn't see words appear differently, but behind the scenes each spoken step now carries a distinct identifier instead of just a placeholder.

ai.title: Add fast best-of-n agent variant
ai.summary: Introduce `bestOfNFast` option in `createBase2` to enable a new fast best-of-n workflow. Adds `base2-best-of-n-fast-orchestrator`, `base2-best-of-n-fast`, and `base2-selector-fast` agents. Orchestrator spawns five `base2-implementor-step` agents and uses `base2-selector-fast` to pick the best implementation. Selector uses `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` and outputs only the `implementationId`.

eli5.text: You now have a faster way to generate multiple solutions to the same coding task and pick the best one. When the base2 assistant is set to the 'fast' mode with the best-of-n option, it spawns five parallel implementor agents and then uses Claude Sonnet 4.5 to evaluate and select the single best implementation, outputting only that implementation's ID. This new fast variant is live today for anyone using the fast best-of-n workflow, alongside the existing slower best-of-n option.

ai.title: Refactor best-of-n agent definitions and IDs
ai.summary: Renamed agent IDs and files to drop the `base2-` prefix (e.g., `base2-best-of-n-orchestrator` becomes `best-of-n-orchestrator`). Deleted redundant `base2-best-of-n-editor`, `base2-selector`, and `base2-implementor-step-gpt-5` files, consolidating logic into `best-of-n-implementor.ts` and `best-of-n-selector.ts`. Updated `createBase2` in `base2.ts` to reference the new orchestrator IDs and spawnable agents. This internal cleanup removes legacy naming conventions and simplifies the agent definition structure.

eli5.text: The company cleaned up the internal naming of its coding assistants, dropping an old prefix so the assistant names are now simpler and easier to read. Three duplicate helper files were removed and their useful parts were merged into two main files. Since this only affects how things are labeled behind the scenes, you won't notice any difference in features or performance.

eli5.text: If your automated code-assistant tests had been stuck or frozen, they now stop automatically after 30 minutes instead of running forever. The timer now covers the entire test process, including setting up the code repository, running the assistant, comparing changes, and checking results, not just the part where the assistant writes code. This prevents stuck tests from hogging resources indefinitely. It's a behind-the-scenes safety net for the team that builds and runs these evaluation tests.

ai.title: Update buffbench log analyzer to exclude zero-score tasks
ai.summary: Refactors scripts/analyze-buffbench-logs.ts to implement a two-pass analysis strategy. The first pass identifies tasks where any agent received a zero or null overall score, excluding these from the final metrics to prevent skewed averages. The bottom-25% filtering logic was updated to calculate a global cutoff across all agents rather than per-agent, ensuring consistent task exclusion. The script now returns both aggregated results and raw agent scores, printing the latter to the console for deeper inspection.

eli5.text: The BuffBench log analysis tool now automatically skips any task where an agent received a score of zero or no score at all, then recalculates the bottom-25% cutoff across all remaining agents at once instead of per-agent, and prints every agent's raw scores to the console for closer inspection. If you run the analyzer, you will see a note telling you how many tasks were excluded because an agent scored zero or blank, and the low-performer filtering will drop entire tasks whenever any agent in that task fell below the global cutoff rather than just dropping individual agent entries. The raw score printout lets you verify the filtering yourself, but the averages and rankings will reflect only the surviving, non-zero-scoring tasks.
